claim: Label-noise ceiling: with a measurement-error model y = t + e, the maximum R2 any model can score against noisy labels is 1 - sigma_e^2/sigma_y^2. Using sigma_e = 0.68 log units for heterogeneous public pIC50, the ceiling is R2 = 0.54 / 0.68 / 0.79 / 0.88 for label spreads sigma_y = 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.5 / 2.0 log units, and the RMSE floor is 0.68 log units (about 4.8-fold in potency).
source_title: Derived label-noise ceiling on QSAR model accuracy

figures.metric: maximum achievable R2 against noisy public pIC50 labels
figures.denominator_def: R2 measured against experimentally observed (noisy) labels, not against true values
figures.sample: derived from published pIC50 replicate spread

derivation: Assume y = t + e, e independent of t, Var(e)=sigma_e^2, Var(y)=sigma_y^2. A model predicting t perfectly has residual variance sigma_e^2 against y, so R2_max = 1 - sigma_e^2/sigma_y^2 and r_max = sqrt(R2_max). Inputs: sigma_e = 0.68 [E-7022]; sigma_e = 0.54 for curated Ki [E-7021]. sigma_y swept over 1.0-2.0 log units because the label spread of a QSAR set is dataset-specific and was not sourced. Results: sigma_e=0.68 -> R2_max 0.538 (sigma_y=1.0), 0.679 (1.2), 0.794 (1.5), 0.884 (2.0). sigma_e=0.54 -> R2_max 0.709 (1.0), 0.797 (1.2), 0.870 (1.5), 0.927 (2.0). RMSE floor = sigma_e. Caveat from [E-7023]: the true-value error can be lower than this apparent ceiling; the ceiling binds measured benchmark scores, not necessarily real utility.

figures.metric: R = AI design generation capacity / experimental validation capacity, de novo binder design
figures.unit: designs generated per design tested per year
figures.denominator_def: numerator = backbone+sequence designs generatable per year on one GPU node; denominator = designs expressed and assayed per year by the same organisation

derivation: Numerator: 1040 backbones / 1.9 GPU-h = 547/GPU-h [E-7029]. One 8-GPU node at 60% duty = 547*8*0.6*8760 = 2.3e7 designs/yr; a conservative single-GPU figure is 547*0.6*8760 = 2.9e6/yr. Take numerator 3e6 (single GPU, group scale) to 2e7 (8-GPU node, platform scale). Denominator: protein expression/purification runs 96 in parallel, hundreds per week per operator [E-7048][E-7049]; at 300/week x 48 weeks = 1.44e4/yr for a dedicated platform, and 10-20 designs/target on frontier campaigns [E-7050][E-7053] implies a few hundred to ~1e3/yr for a single group. Group scale: 3e6/5e2 = 6.0e3. Platform scale: 2e7/1.44e4 = 1.4e3. Taking a central band across settings R ~ 5e2-2e3 with outer bound 1e2-1e4. The numerator is bounded only by compute budget, so R has no upper limit in principle; the figure above uses one modest GPU node.

derivation: Numerator: 3.6e10 compounds addressed per V-SYNTHES2 campaign [E-7057][E-7032]; one campaign per year taken as the unit. Denominator (a) nominal: 1e5 compounds/day industrial HTS [E-7033] x 200 operating days = 2.0e7 wells/yr -> R = 3.6e10/2.0e7 = 1.8e3. At 1536-well 2e5/day x 200 = 4.0e7 -> R = 9.0e2. Denominator (b) effective: a hit-to-lead program on a ~1-week DMTA cycle [E-7045] with make-on-demand batches [E-7032] physically makes and tests on the order of 5e3 novel designed compounds/yr -> R = 3.6e10/5e3 = 7.2e6. The two denominators differ by ~4000x, which is the nominal-vs-effective gap: HTS wells re-test an existing deck rather than testing the designed molecules.

claim: Design-surplus ratio R for antibody affinity maturation is below 1 when pooled display selection counts as validation (R about 0.1) but 10^5 to 10^6 when validation is restricted to per-variant biophysical characterisation.
source_title: Derived design-surplus ratio, antibody affinity maturation workflow

figures.metric: R = designs generated / variants meaningfully tested, antibody affinity maturation
figures.unit: ratio against pooled display capacity (1e5-1e6 against per-variant biophysics)
figures.denominator_def: numerator = designed antibody sequences generatable per year; denominators = (a) library members interrogated per display selection, (b) variants with individually measured affinity/expression/developability
figures.sample: yeast/phage display practice vs generative antibody design

derivation: Numerator: sequence-level generative models are cheaper per sample than structure diffusion [E-7029]; taking a conservative 1e8 designed sequences per year for one group. Denominator (a): display libraries interrogate 1e9 variants per selection [E-7054] -> R = 1e8/1e9 = 0.1. Denominator (b): only sorted leads receive individual SPR/BLI measurement [E-7054]; at 1e2-1e3 variants individually characterised per year -> R = 1e8/1e3 = 1e5 to 1e8/1e2 = 1e6. The pooled-display readout is an enrichment score confounded by expression and avidity, so it is high-throughput but low-information per variant.

claim: Elasticity comparison: using the published decision-theoretic result that +0.1 absolute predictive validity beats a 10x throughput gain, a 10% wet-lab throughput improvement is worth about +0.0041 of predictive validity, whereas a 10% relative improvement in predictive validity from a base r of 0.3-0.6 is worth 0.03-0.06 - making assay validity roughly 7 to 15 times (central 12x) more elastic than throughput for the same proportional effort.
source_title: Derived elasticity comparison, throughput vs predictive validity

figures.metric: predictive-validity equivalent of a 10 percent throughput gain
figures.denominator_def: equivalence derived from the published statement that +0.1 correlation exceeds a 10x (i.e. +900%) throughput change

derivation: From [E-7061], delta_r = 0.1 is at least as valuable as a factor-10 throughput change. Treating the throughput benefit as approximately logarithmic (in the rare-positive regime the number of candidates that must be screened per true positive scales with log throughput), the validity-equivalent of a throughput factor f is delta_r_eq = 0.1 * ln(f)/ln(10). For f = 1.1 (a 10 percent throughput gain): 0.1 * 0.09531/2.30259 = 0.00414. A 10 percent relative improvement in predictive validity gives delta_r = 0.03 at r=0.3, 0.04 at r=0.4, 0.05 at r=0.5, 0.06 at r=0.6. Ratios: 0.03/0.00414 = 7.2; 0.04/0.00414 = 9.7; 0.05/0.00414 = 12.1; 0.06/0.00414 = 14.5. Hence validity is 7-15x (central ~12x) more elastic than throughput for equal proportional effort. If the throughput benefit saturates rather than remaining logarithmic, the multiple is larger; if it were linear in f the multiple would fall below 1, but a linear reading contradicts the source statement in [E-7061] that +0.1 correlation outperforms a full 10x throughput change. This is a derived elasticity from a published simulation, not a measured elasticity on approval counts.

claim: Validation capacity is not uniformly scarce: nominal test capacity exceeds design capacity in antibody display (R about 0.1) while falling three to seven orders of magnitude short in binder design and small-molecule synthesis, so 'validation throughput' is not a single quantity.
source_title: Derived cross-workflow comparison of design-surplus ratios

figures.metric: spread of R across three workflows

derivation: Minimum R across workflows = 0.1 [E-7105, pooled display]; maximum R = 7.2e6 [E-7104, novel-compound synthesis]. log10(7.2e6/0.1) = 7.86, i.e. roughly 7-8 orders of magnitude of spread. A single 'design surplus' figure for AI-driven discovery therefore cannot be quoted without naming the workflow and the definition of a tested design.

claim: Over a full 15-year window the gene synthesis list price fell roughly 19-fold, from about $1.30 per base for simple genes circa 2010-2011 to $0.07 per bp in 2025, an average decline of about 19% per year - materially slower than the exponential decline often assumed, and with most of the fall concentrated after 2017.
source_title: Derived 15-year gene synthesis cost trajectory

figures.metric: 15-year fold decline in gene synthesis list price
figures.denominator_def: quoted commercial price per base for synthesised genes/fragments at each endpoint

derivation: 1.30 [E-7065] / 0.07 [E-7030] = 18.57 over ~14.5 years -> (0.07/1.30)^(1/14.5) = 0.8127, i.e. 18.7% average annual decline. Using the raw-oligo figure 0.10 [E-7065] instead gives 0.10/0.07 = 1.43 over 14.5 years, i.e. 2.5% per year, so the two 2010-11 anchors bracket the true series widely. The 2017-2025 sub-window measured on like-for-like vendor gene-fragment pricing is 14.8-23.8% per year [E-7102]. The 2010-11 endpoint is a secondary compilation of the Carlson series, not the primary series, so the 15-year figure is an estimate with a wide band (2.5-19% per year) while the 8-year figure [E-7102] rests on two directly retrieved vendor statements.
